title: Trace-zero injectivity of the Conjecture 12 quadrinomial
summary: Decide whether the Mesnager--Yuan--Zheng quadrinomial is injective on the absolute-trace-zero subset in every odd extension degree of its family.

formal_statement.body: For each source-admissible positive integer $m$, put $n=2m+1$ and define $$F_m(x)=x+x^3+x^{2^{m+1}}+x^{2^{m+1}+2}$$ on $\mathbb F_{2^n}$. Let $T_0=\{x\in\mathbb F_{2^n}:\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathbb F_{2^n}/\mathbb F_2}(x)=0\}$. Prove that $F_m|_{T_0}$ is injective for every admissible $m$, or exhibit an admissible $m$ and distinct $x,y\in T_0$ with $F_m(x)=F_m(y)$.

scope.domain: Restrictions of finite-field vectorial functions used to construct cryptographic involutions and S-boxes
assumptions: $n=2m+1$ with $m$ in the source-admissible positive-integer range
$F_m$ is the exact quadrinomial in Conjecture 12
$T_0$ is the absolute-trace-zero subset of $\mathbb F_{2^n}$
scope.unresolved_remainder: The full-field two-to-one branch of Conjecture 12 has been proved, but no inspected later result shows that each two-point fiber contains at most one trace-zero element. Injectivity on $T_0$ remains open over the complete source parameter range.

progress.summary: Conjecture 12 asserts that the displayed two-to-one quadrinomial is injective on the absolute-trace-zero set for every member of the family.
